title: iPhone to Android File Transfer - OneSync App & Web
description: Send files and text between iPhone, Android and any computer browser. Start a session, scan a QR code or enter a code. No account, no cable.
h1: iPhone and Android file transfer, without cables or accounts
tagline: Send files and text between your phone, tablet and computer, with no cable and no account.
summary: OneSync sends files and text between iPhone, Android phones and tablets, and any computer through a web browser. There is no account, no cable and no pairing.
It is made for people who move a photo, a document or a copied link between devices that cannot use AirDrop together, such as an iPhone and an Android tablet, or a work PC and a phone.
You start a session on one device, then other devices join by scanning a QR code or entering a code. Every device in the session receives what you send.
overview: iPhone to Android file transfer is awkward because AirDrop does not cross platforms and cables need the right adapter. OneSync works through a temporary session instead. Open the app on one device and start a session to get a QR code and a short session code. On another device, scan the QR code or type the code. On a computer you do not install anything: open the OneSync web client in a browser, such as onesync.setlog.net, and join the same way.

Once devices are in the session, you can send files and text to all of them. You can share straight from other apps through the share sheet, copy a link or a sentence on one device and receive it on another, and join with a QR code, a code or a link. Large file transfers can resume after a network interruption.

OneSync is a temporary transfer channel for hand-offs. Transfers go through our server over encrypted connections (HTTPS/TLS), and files and text are deleted from the server after the session ends. That makes it suitable for quick hand-offs on a shared PC or between family members' phones, and unsuitable for highly sensitive files.

features.h: Transfer files between iPhone and Android
features.p: Start a session on an iPhone or an Android phone and let the other device join with the QR code or session code. Files you send arrive on every device in the session. Each session also shows a short verification number so you can confirm you joined the right one.

features.h: A web client for any computer
features.p: Computers join through a browser, so there is nothing to install on a Windows PC, Mac or Linux machine. The session screen shows the PC web address, and you can copy it. The QR scan screen explains how to show the QR code on your PC.

features.h: Send text and links as well as files
features.p: Share a copied sentence or link to every device in the session. Everything you send is listed in the session activity, so you can download or copy it on each device.

features.h: Share from other apps and join with a link
features.p: Use the share sheet to send a photo or document from another app straight into your session. Join by QR code, by entering a code, or by opening a link.

features.h: No account, and sessions clean up after themselves
features.p: There is no sign-up and no login. The session screen shows the time remaining, and when a session ends, the files and text in it are deleted from the server.

specs.v: iPhone and iPad (iOS 15 or later), Android, and any computer through a web browser
QR code, session code or link, with a short verification number; no sign-up or login
Files and text; share from other apps through the share sheet
Larger files, longer sessions, more devices in one session and no ads

limits: OneSync does not use end-to-end encryption, so do not use it for highly sensitive files. Transfers use HTTPS/TLS and pass through our server.
It is a temporary channel. Sessions end, and files and text are deleted from the server afterwards, so it does not keep files for months.
Each session runs for a set time shown on the session screen. When it ends, start a new session on any device for the next transfer.
Computers use the web client in a browser; the store listing describes no separate app for Windows, Mac or Linux.
Both people need a connection to the internet, because files travel through our server on their way between devices.

faq.q: How do I transfer files from iPhone to Android?
faq.a: Open OneSync on one device and start a session to get a QR code and a code. Scan the QR code or enter the code on the other device, then send files and text. Every device in the session receives them.

faq.q: Can I send files to a PC without installing anything?
faq.a: Yes. Open the OneSync web client in any browser, for example onesync.setlog.net, and join the session with the QR code or the code. The session screen in the app shows the PC web address.

faq.q: Do I need an account or a cable?
faq.a: No. There is no sign-up, login, cable or pairing. A session is created on one device and joined by QR code, code or link.

Yes. Large file transfers can resume after a network interruption, so a dropped connection does not send you back to the start. The session screen shows the time remaining, and Pro (optional) adds larger files and longer sessions.

faq.q: Is OneSync secure and what happens to my files?
faq.a: Transfers use encrypted connections (HTTPS/TLS), and files and text are deleted from the server after the session ends. OneSync does not use end-to-end encryption, so avoid sharing highly sensitive files.

faq.q: Which devices can join one session?
faq.a: iPhone, iPad and Android devices join through the app, and any computer joins through the web client in a browser. Everything you send reaches each device in the session. Pro (optional) lets more devices join the same session.
